1.q: Find the real and imaginary parts of $z=\left(4-3i\right)^{-2}$.
1.solution:
Let $z=(4-3i)^{-2}$. Rewrite the negative exponent as a reciprocal.

$$z=\frac{1}{(4-3i)^2}$$

Expand the square, keeping the middle term.

$$\begin{aligned}(4-3i)^2 &= 4^2-2(4)(3i)+(3i)^2 && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small (a-b)^2=a^2-2ab+b^2} \\ &= 16-24i+9i^2 \\ &= 16-24i+9(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= (16-9)-24i \\ &= 7-24i\end{aligned}$$

Substitute the square into the denominator. Write the reciprocal and use the conjugate $7+24i$.

$$\begin{aligned}z &= \frac{1}{7-24i} \\ &= \frac{1}{7-24i}\cdot\frac{7+24i}{7+24i} && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \frac{7+24i}{7+24i}=1} \\ &= \frac{7+24i}{(7-24i)(7+24i)}\end{aligned}$$

Multiply the conjugate pair using the difference of squares.

$$\begin{aligned}(7-24i)(7+24i) &= 7^2-(24i)^2 && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small (a+b)(a-b)=a^2-b^2} \\ &= 49-576i^2 \\ &= 49-576(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 49+576 \\ &= 625\end{aligned}$$

Substitute the numerator and denominator, then simplify to rectangular form.

$$\begin{aligned}z &= \frac{7+24i}{625} \\ &= \frac{7}{625}+\frac{24}{625}i\end{aligned}$$

Read the real coefficient and the coefficient of $i$.

$$\begin{gathered}\operatorname{Re}(z)=\dfrac{7}{625} \\ \operatorname{Im}(z)=\dfrac{24}{625}\end{gathered}$$
$\mathrm{Re}(z)=\dfrac{7}{625}$ and $\mathrm{Im}(z)=\dfrac{24}{625}$

$$\begin{aligned}(2+i)(2+i) &= 2(2)+2(i)+(i)(2)+(i)(i) \\ &= 4+2i+2i+i^2 \\ &= 4+2i+2i+1(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 4+2i+2i-1 \\ &= (4-1)+(2+2)i && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{collect like terms}} \\ &= 3+4i\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}w &= \frac{-1+5i}{-1+i} \\ &= \frac{-1+5i}{-1+i}\cdot\frac{-1-i}{-1-i} && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \frac{-1-i}{-1-i}=1} \\ &= \frac{(-1+5i)(-1-i)}{(-1+i)(-1-i)}\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}(-1+5i)(-1-i) &= (-1)(-1)+(-1)(-i)+(5i)(-1)+(5i)(-i) \\ &= 1+i-5i-5i^2 \\ &= 1+i-5i-5(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 1+i-5i+5 \\ &= (1+5)+(1-5)i && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{collect like terms}} \\ &= 6-4i\end{aligned}$$

Multiply the conjugate pair using the difference of squares.

$$\begin{aligned}(-1+i)(-1-i) &= (-1)^2-i^2 && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small (a+b)(a-b)=a^2-b^2} \\ &= 1-i^2 \\ &= 1-1(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 1+1 \\ &= 2\end{aligned}$$

$$z=-1-i-w$$

$$\begin{aligned}(2)(-1-i-w)+(3+i)w&=9-i \\ (-2-2i)+((3+i)-2)w&=9-i \\ (1+i)w&=(9-i)-(-2-2i) \\ (1+i)w&=11+i\end{aligned}$$

Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate $1-i$.

$$\begin{aligned}w &= \frac{11+i}{1+i} \\ &= \frac{11+i}{1+i}\cdot\frac{1-i}{1-i} && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \frac{1-i}{1-i}=1} \\ &= \frac{(11+i)(1-i)}{(1+i)(1-i)}\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}(11+i)(1-i) &= 11(1)+11(-i)+(i)(1)+(i)(-i) \\ &= 11-11i+i-i^2 \\ &= 11-11i+i-1(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 11-11i+i+1 \\ &= (11+1)+(-11+1)i && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{collect like terms}} \\ &= 12-10i\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}(1+i)(1-i) &= 1^2-i^2 && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small (a+b)(a-b)=a^2-b^2} \\ &= 1-i^2 \\ &= 1-1(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 1+1 \\ &= 2\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}w &= \frac{-2-4i}{-2i} \\ &= \frac{-2-4i}{-2i}\cdot\frac{2i}{2i} && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \frac{2i}{2i}=1} \\ &= \frac{(-2-4i)(2i)}{(-2i)(2i)}\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}(-2i)(2i) &= 0^2-(2i)^2 && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small (a+b)(a-b)=a^2-b^2} \\ &= 0-4i^2 \\ &= 0-4(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 0+4 \\ &= 4\end{aligned}$$

Both equations are satisfied.

$$\begin{gathered}z=1+2i \\ w=2-i\end{gathered}$$
$z=1+2i$ and $w=2-i$

Subtract the first scaled equation from the second. The $x$ terms cancel.

$$\begin{aligned}(-4-1)y&=8-3 \\ -5y&=5 \\ y&=\frac{5}{-5} \\ y&=-1\end{aligned}$$

Substitute $y=-1$ into $(1)$ and solve for $x$.

1.q: Solve $\left(2+3i\right)(a+bi)=7+4i$ for the real numbers $a$ and $b$.
1.solution:
Expand the product, replacing $i^2$ by $-1$.

$$\begin{aligned}(2+3i)(a+bi) &= 2a+2bi+3ai+3bi^2 \\ &= (2a-3b)+(3a+2b)i && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1}\end{aligned}$$

The unknowns are real. Match the two coefficients to obtain

$$\begin{aligned}2a-3b&=7\qquad\cdots(1) \\ 3a+2b&=4\qquad\cdots(2)\end{aligned}$$

Multiply $(1)$ by $3$ and $(2)$ by $2$ to give matching $a$ coefficients.

$$\begin{aligned}6a-9b&=21 \\ 6a+4b&=8\end{aligned}$$

Subtract the first scaled equation from the second. The $a$ terms cancel.

$$\begin{aligned}(4-(-9))b&=8-21 \\ 13b&=-13 \\ b&=\frac{-13}{13} \\ b&=-1\end{aligned}$$

Substitute $b=-1$ into $(1)$ and solve for $a$.

$$\begin{aligned}2a+(-3)(-1)&=7 \\ 2a&=7-3 \\ 2a&=4 \\ a&=\frac{4}{2} \\ a&=2\end{aligned}$$

Check the values in the collected complex equation.

$$\begin{aligned}(2+3i)(2)+(-3+2i)(-1) &= (4+6i)+(3-2i) \\ &= 7+4i\end{aligned}$$

The required values are

$$\begin{gathered}a=2 \\ b=-1\end{gathered}$$
$a=2$ and $b=-1$

$$\begin{aligned}z_1(z_2+z_3) &= (1+i)(3-3i) \\ &= 1(3)+1(-3i)+(i)(3)+(i)(-3i) \\ &= 3-3i+3i-3i^2 \\ &= 3-3i+3i-3(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 3-3i+3i+3 \\ &= (3+3)+(-3+3)i && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{collect like terms}} \\ &= 6\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}z_1z_2 &= (1+i)(2-i) \\ &= 1(2)+1(-i)+(i)(2)+(i)(-i) \\ &= 2-i+2i-i^2 \\ &= 2-i+2i-1(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 2-i+2i+1 \\ &= (2+1)+(-1+2)i && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{collect like terms}} \\ &= 3+i\end{aligned}$$

1.q: For $z_1=2+i$ and $z_2=1-2i$, verify $\overline{(z_1/z_2)}=\bar z_1/\bar z_2$ by calculating both sides.
1.solution:
Calculate the left side first: perform the operation before conjugating. Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate $1+2i$.

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{z_1}{z_2} &= \frac{2+i}{1-2i} \\ &= \frac{2+i}{1-2i}\cdot\frac{1+2i}{1+2i} && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \frac{1+2i}{1+2i}=1} \\ &= \frac{(2+i)(1+2i)}{(1-2i)(1+2i)}\end{aligned}$$

Expand the numerator first.

$$\begin{aligned}(2+i)(1+2i) &= 2(1)+2(2i)+(i)(1)+(i)(2i) \\ &= 2+4i+i+2i^2 \\ &= 2+4i+i+2(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 2+4i+i-2 \\ &= (2-2)+(4+1)i && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{collect like terms}} \\ &= 5i\end{aligned}$$

Multiply the conjugate pair using the difference of squares.

$$\begin{aligned}(1-2i)(1+2i) &= 1^2-(2i)^2 && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small (a+b)(a-b)=a^2-b^2} \\ &= 1-4i^2 \\ &= 1-4(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 1+4 \\ &= 5\end{aligned}$$

Substitute the numerator and denominator, then simplify to rectangular form.

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{z_1}{z_2} &= \frac{5i}{5} \\ &= \frac{5}{5}i \\ &= i\end{aligned}$$

Take the conjugate of this result.

$$\begin{aligned}\overline{\frac{z_1}{z_2}} &= \overline{i} \\ &= -i\end{aligned}$$

For the right side, conjugate the two inputs first.

$$\begin{gathered}\bar z_1=2-i \\ \bar z_2=1+2i\end{gathered}$$

Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate $1-2i$.

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{\bar z_1}{\bar z_2} &= \frac{2-i}{1+2i} \\ &= \frac{2-i}{1+2i}\cdot\frac{1-2i}{1-2i} && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \frac{1-2i}{1-2i}=1} \\ &= \frac{(2-i)(1-2i)}{(1+2i)(1-2i)}\end{aligned}$$

Expand the numerator first.

$$\begin{aligned}(2-i)(1-2i) &= 2(1)+2(-2i)+(-i)(1)+(-i)(-2i) \\ &= 2-4i-i+2i^2 \\ &= 2-4i-i+2(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 2-4i-i-2 \\ &= (2-2)+(-4-1)i && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{collect like terms}} \\ &= -5i\end{aligned}$$

Multiply the conjugate pair using the difference of squares.

$$\begin{aligned}(1+2i)(1-2i) &= 1^2-(2i)^2 && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small (a+b)(a-b)=a^2-b^2} \\ &= 1-4i^2 \\ &= 1-4(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 1+4 \\ &= 5\end{aligned}$$

Substitute the numerator and denominator, then simplify to rectangular form.

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{\bar z_1}{\bar z_2} &= \frac{-5i}{5} \\ &= -\frac{5}{5}i \\ &= -i\end{aligned}$$

Both sides give $-i$, so the required equality holds for these values.

$$\overline{\frac{z_1}{z_2}}=\frac{\bar z_1}{\bar z_2}=-i$$
Both sides give $-i$.

1.q: For $z_1=3-i$ and $z_2=2+i$, verify $\overline{(z_1/z_2)}=\bar z_1/\bar z_2$ by calculating both sides.
1.solution:
Calculate the left side first: perform the operation before conjugating. Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate $2-i$.

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{z_1}{z_2} &= \frac{3-i}{2+i} \\ &= \frac{3-i}{2+i}\cdot\frac{2-i}{2-i} && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \frac{2-i}{2-i}=1} \\ &= \frac{(3-i)(2-i)}{(2+i)(2-i)}\end{aligned}$$

Expand the numerator first.

$$\begin{aligned}(3-i)(2-i) &= 3(2)+3(-i)+(-i)(2)+(-i)(-i) \\ &= 6-3i-2i+i^2 \\ &= 6-3i-2i+1(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 6-3i-2i-1 \\ &= (6-1)+(-3-2)i && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{collect like terms}} \\ &= 5-5i\end{aligned}$$

Multiply the conjugate pair using the difference of squares.

$$\begin{aligned}(2+i)(2-i) &= 2^2-i^2 && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small (a+b)(a-b)=a^2-b^2} \\ &= 4-i^2 \\ &= 4-1(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 4+1 \\ &= 5\end{aligned}$$

Substitute the numerator and denominator, then simplify to rectangular form.

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{z_1}{z_2} &= \frac{5-5i}{5} \\ &= \frac{5(1-i)}{5(1)} && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{cancel the common factor }5} \\ &= 1-i\end{aligned}$$

Take the conjugate of this result.

$$\begin{aligned}\overline{\frac{z_1}{z_2}} &= \overline{1-i} \\ &= 1+i\end{aligned}$$

For the right side, conjugate the two inputs first.

$$\begin{gathered}\bar z_1=3+i \\ \bar z_2=2-i\end{gathered}$$

Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate $2+i$.

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{\bar z_1}{\bar z_2} &= \frac{3+i}{2-i} \\ &= \frac{3+i}{2-i}\cdot\frac{2+i}{2+i} && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \frac{2+i}{2+i}=1} \\ &= \frac{(3+i)(2+i)}{(2-i)(2+i)}\end{aligned}$$

Expand the numerator first.

$$\begin{aligned}(3+i)(2+i) &= 3(2)+3(i)+(i)(2)+(i)(i) \\ &= 6+3i+2i+i^2 \\ &= 6+3i+2i+1(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 6+3i+2i-1 \\ &= (6-1)+(3+2)i && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{collect like terms}} \\ &= 5+5i\end{aligned}$$

Multiply the conjugate pair using the difference of squares.

$$\begin{aligned}(2-i)(2+i) &= 2^2-i^2 && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small (a+b)(a-b)=a^2-b^2} \\ &= 4-i^2 \\ &= 4-1(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 4+1 \\ &= 5\end{aligned}$$

Substitute the numerator and denominator, then simplify to rectangular form.

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{\bar z_1}{\bar z_2} &= \frac{5+5i}{5} \\ &= \frac{5(1+i)}{5(1)} && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{cancel the common factor }5} \\ &= 1+i\end{aligned}$$

Both sides give $1+i$, so the required equality holds for these values.

$$\overline{\frac{z_1}{z_2}}=\frac{\bar z_1}{\bar z_2}=1+i$$
Both sides give $1+i$.

1.q: For $z_1=-1+3i$ and $z_2=2-i$, verify $\overline{(z_1/z_2)}=\bar z_1/\bar z_2$ by calculating both sides.
1.solution:
Calculate the left side first: perform the operation before conjugating. Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate $2+i$.

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{z_1}{z_2} &= \frac{-1+3i}{2-i} \\ &= \frac{-1+3i}{2-i}\cdot\frac{2+i}{2+i} && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \frac{2+i}{2+i}=1} \\ &= \frac{(-1+3i)(2+i)}{(2-i)(2+i)}\end{aligned}$$

Expand the numerator first.

$$\begin{aligned}(-1+3i)(2+i) &= (-1)(2)+(-1)(i)+(3i)(2)+(3i)(i) \\ &= -2-i+6i+3i^2 \\ &= -2-i+6i+3(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= -2-i+6i-3 \\ &= (-2-3)+(-1+6)i && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{collect like terms}} \\ &= -5+5i\end{aligned}$$

Multiply the conjugate pair using the difference of squares.

$$\begin{aligned}(2-i)(2+i) &= 2^2-i^2 && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small (a+b)(a-b)=a^2-b^2} \\ &= 4-i^2 \\ &= 4-1(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 4+1 \\ &= 5\end{aligned}$$

Substitute the numerator and denominator, then simplify to rectangular form.

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{z_1}{z_2} &= \frac{-5+5i}{5} \\ &= \frac{5(-1+i)}{5(1)} && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{cancel the common factor }5} \\ &= -1+i\end{aligned}$$

Take the conjugate of this result.

$$\begin{aligned}\overline{\frac{z_1}{z_2}} &= \overline{-1+i} \\ &= -1-i\end{aligned}$$

For the right side, conjugate the two inputs first.

$$\begin{gathered}\bar z_1=-1-3i \\ \bar z_2=2+i\end{gathered}$$

Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate $2-i$.

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{\bar z_1}{\bar z_2} &= \frac{-1-3i}{2+i} \\ &= \frac{-1-3i}{2+i}\cdot\frac{2-i}{2-i} && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \frac{2-i}{2-i}=1} \\ &= \frac{(-1-3i)(2-i)}{(2+i)(2-i)}\end{aligned}$$

Expand the numerator first.

$$\begin{aligned}(-1-3i)(2-i) &= (-1)(2)+(-1)(-i)+(-3i)(2)+(-3i)(-i) \\ &= -2+i-6i+3i^2 \\ &= -2+i-6i+3(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= -2+i-6i-3 \\ &= (-2-3)+(1-6)i && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{collect like terms}} \\ &= -5-5i\end{aligned}$$

Multiply the conjugate pair using the difference of squares.

$$\begin{aligned}(2+i)(2-i) &= 2^2-i^2 && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small (a+b)(a-b)=a^2-b^2} \\ &= 4-i^2 \\ &= 4-1(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 4+1 \\ &= 5\end{aligned}$$

Substitute the numerator and denominator, then simplify to rectangular form.

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{\bar z_1}{\bar z_2} &= \frac{-5-5i}{5} \\ &= \frac{5(-1-i)}{5(1)} && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{cancel the common factor }5} \\ &= -1-i\end{aligned}$$

Both sides give $-1-i$, so the required equality holds for these values.

$$\overline{\frac{z_1}{z_2}}=\frac{\bar z_1}{\bar z_2}=-1-i$$
Both sides give $-1-i$.

1.solution:
Label the original equations.

$$\begin{aligned}(1+i)z+(2-i)w&=7+4i\qquad\cdots(1) \\ (2+i)z+(1-i)w&=8+i\qquad\cdots(2)\end{aligned}$$

Multiply $(1)$ by $2+i$ and $(2)$ by $1+i$. Subtract the first scaled equation from the second.

$$\begin{aligned}(1+3i)z+5w&=10+15i \\ (1+3i)z+2w&=7+9i\end{aligned}$$

Subtract the first scaled equation from the second; the $z$-terms cancel.

$$\begin{aligned}((2)-5)w&=(7+9i)-(10+15i) \\ (-3)w&=-3-6i\end{aligned}$$

The denominator is real and nonzero. Divide each coefficient.

$$\begin{aligned}w &= \frac{-3-6i}{-3} \\ &= \frac{3+6i}{3} \\ &= \frac{3(1+2i)}{3(1)} && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{cancel the common factor }3} \\ &= 1+2i\end{aligned}$$

Substitute $w=1+2i$ into $(1)$.

$$(1+i)z+(2-i)(1+2i)=7+4i$$

Evaluate the known product before isolating $z$.

$$\begin{aligned}(2-i)(1+2i) &= 2(1)+2(2i)+(-i)(1)+(-i)(2i) \\ &= 2+4i-i-2i^2 \\ &= 2+4i-i-2(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 2+4i-i+2 \\ &= (2+2)+(4-1)i && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{collect like terms}} \\ &= 4+3i\end{aligned}$$

Subtract the known term.

$$\begin{aligned}(1+i)z&=(7+4i)-(4+3i) \\ (1+i)z&=3+i\end{aligned}$$

Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate $1-i$.

$$\begin{aligned}z &= \frac{3+i}{1+i} \\ &= \frac{3+i}{1+i}\cdot\frac{1-i}{1-i} && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \frac{1-i}{1-i}=1} \\ &= \frac{(3+i)(1-i)}{(1+i)(1-i)}\end{aligned}$$

Expand the numerator first.

$$\begin{aligned}(3+i)(1-i) &= 3(1)+3(-i)+(i)(1)+(i)(-i) \\ &= 3-3i+i-i^2 \\ &= 3-3i+i-1(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 3-3i+i+1 \\ &= (3+1)+(-3+1)i && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{collect like terms}} \\ &= 4-2i\end{aligned}$$

Multiply the conjugate pair using the difference of squares.

$$\begin{aligned}(1+i)(1-i) &= 1^2-i^2 && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small (a+b)(a-b)=a^2-b^2} \\ &= 1-i^2 \\ &= 1-1(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 1+1 \\ &= 2\end{aligned}$$

Substitute the numerator and denominator, then simplify to rectangular form.

$$\begin{aligned}z &= \frac{4-2i}{2} \\ &= \frac{2(2-i)}{2(1)} && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{cancel the common factor }2} \\ &= 2-i\end{aligned}$$

Check the first original equation.

$$\begin{aligned}(1+i)(2-i)+(2-i)(1+2i) &= (3+i)+(4+3i) \\ &= 7+4i\end{aligned}$$

Check the second original equation with the same values.

$$\begin{aligned}(2+i)(2-i)+(1-i)(1+2i) &= (5)+(3+i) \\ &= 8+i\end{aligned}$$

Both equations are satisfied.

$$\begin{gathered}z=2-i \\ w=1+2i\end{gathered}$$
$z=2-i$ and $w=1+2i$

1.solution:
Label the original equations.

$$\begin{aligned}(2-i)z+(1+2i)w&=3+6i\qquad\cdots(1) \\ (1-i)z+(3+i)w&=7+i\qquad\cdots(2)\end{aligned}$$

Multiply $(1)$ by $1-i$ and $(2)$ by $2-i$. Subtract the first scaled equation from the second.

$$\begin{aligned}(1-3i)z+(3+i)w&=9+3i \\ (1-3i)z+(7-i)w&=15-5i\end{aligned}$$

Subtract the first scaled equation from the second; the $z$-terms cancel.

$$\begin{aligned}((7-i)-(3+i))w&=(15-5i)-(9+3i) \\ (4-2i)w&=6-8i\end{aligned}$$

Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate $4+2i$.

$$\begin{aligned}w &= \frac{6-8i}{4-2i} \\ &= \frac{6-8i}{4-2i}\cdot\frac{4+2i}{4+2i} && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \frac{4+2i}{4+2i}=1} \\ &= \frac{(6-8i)(4+2i)}{(4-2i)(4+2i)}\end{aligned}$$

Expand the numerator first.

$$\begin{aligned}(6-8i)(4+2i) &= 6(4)+6(2i)+(-8i)(4)+(-8i)(2i) \\ &= 24+12i-32i-16i^2 \\ &= 24+12i-32i-16(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 24+12i-32i+16 \\ &= (24+16)+(12-32)i && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{collect like terms}} \\ &= 40-20i\end{aligned}$$

Multiply the conjugate pair using the difference of squares.

$$\begin{aligned}(4-2i)(4+2i) &= 4^2-(2i)^2 && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small (a+b)(a-b)=a^2-b^2} \\ &= 16-4i^2 \\ &= 16-4(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 16+4 \\ &= 20\end{aligned}$$

Substitute the numerator and denominator, then simplify to rectangular form.

$$\begin{aligned}w &= \frac{40-20i}{20} \\ &= \frac{20(2-i)}{20(1)} && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{cancel the common factor }20} \\ &= 2-i\end{aligned}$$

Substitute $w=2-i$ into $(1)$.

$$(2-i)z+(1+2i)(2-i)=3+6i$$

Evaluate the known product before isolating $z$.

$$\begin{aligned}(1+2i)(2-i) &= 1(2)+1(-i)+(2i)(2)+(2i)(-i) \\ &= 2-i+4i-2i^2 \\ &= 2-i+4i-2(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 2-i+4i+2 \\ &= (2+2)+(-1+4)i && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{collect like terms}} \\ &= 4+3i\end{aligned}$$

Subtract the known term.

$$\begin{aligned}(2-i)z&=(3+6i)-(4+3i) \\ (2-i)z&=-1+3i\end{aligned}$$

Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate $2+i$.

$$\begin{aligned}z &= \frac{-1+3i}{2-i} \\ &= \frac{-1+3i}{2-i}\cdot\frac{2+i}{2+i} && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \frac{2+i}{2+i}=1} \\ &= \frac{(-1+3i)(2+i)}{(2-i)(2+i)}\end{aligned}$$

Expand the numerator first.

$$\begin{aligned}(-1+3i)(2+i) &= (-1)(2)+(-1)(i)+(3i)(2)+(3i)(i) \\ &= -2-i+6i+3i^2 \\ &= -2-i+6i+3(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= -2-i+6i-3 \\ &= (-2-3)+(-1+6)i && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{collect like terms}} \\ &= -5+5i\end{aligned}$$

Multiply the conjugate pair using the difference of squares.

$$\begin{aligned}(2-i)(2+i) &= 2^2-i^2 && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small (a+b)(a-b)=a^2-b^2} \\ &= 4-i^2 \\ &= 4-1(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 4+1 \\ &= 5\end{aligned}$$

Substitute the numerator and denominator, then simplify to rectangular form.

$$\begin{aligned}z &= \frac{-5+5i}{5} \\ &= \frac{5(-1+i)}{5(1)} && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{cancel the common factor }5} \\ &= -1+i\end{aligned}$$

Check the first original equation.

$$\begin{aligned}(2-i)(-1+i)+(1+2i)(2-i) &= (-1+3i)+(4+3i) \\ &= 3+6i\end{aligned}$$

Check the second original equation with the same values.

$$\begin{aligned}(1-i)(-1+i)+(3+i)(2-i) &= (2i)+(7-i) \\ &= 7+i\end{aligned}$$

Both equations are satisfied.

$$\begin{gathered}z=-1+i \\ w=2-i\end{gathered}$$
$z=-1+i$ and $w=2-i$

1.solution:
Label the original equations.

$$\begin{aligned}(1+2i)z+(2+i)w&=4i\qquad\cdots(1) \\ (3-i)z+(1+i)w&=2\qquad\cdots(2)\end{aligned}$$

Multiply $(1)$ by $3-i$ and $(2)$ by $1+2i$. Subtract the first scaled equation from the second.

$$\begin{aligned}(5+5i)z+(7+i)w&=4+12i \\ (5+5i)z+(-1+3i)w&=2+4i\end{aligned}$$

Subtract the first scaled equation from the second; the $z$-terms cancel.

$$\begin{aligned}((-1+3i)-(7+i))w&=(2+4i)-(4+12i) \\ (-8+2i)w&=-2-8i\end{aligned}$$

Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate $-8-2i$.

$$\begin{aligned}w &= \frac{-2-8i}{-8+2i} \\ &= \frac{-2-8i}{-8+2i}\cdot\frac{-8-2i}{-8-2i} && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \frac{-8-2i}{-8-2i}=1} \\ &= \frac{(-2-8i)(-8-2i)}{(-8+2i)(-8-2i)}\end{aligned}$$

Expand the numerator first.

$$\begin{aligned}(-2-8i)(-8-2i) &= (-2)(-8)+(-2)(-2i)+(-8i)(-8)+(-8i)(-2i) \\ &= 16+4i+64i+16i^2 \\ &= 16+4i+64i+16(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 16+4i+64i-16 \\ &= (16-16)+(4+64)i && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{collect like terms}} \\ &= 68i\end{aligned}$$

Multiply the conjugate pair using the difference of squares.

$$\begin{aligned}(-8+2i)(-8-2i) &= (-8)^2-(2i)^2 && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small (a+b)(a-b)=a^2-b^2} \\ &= 64-4i^2 \\ &= 64-4(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 64+4 \\ &= 68\end{aligned}$$

Substitute the numerator and denominator, then simplify to rectangular form.

$$\begin{aligned}w &= \frac{68i}{68} \\ &= \frac{68}{68}i \\ &= i\end{aligned}$$

Substitute $w=i$ into $(1)$.

$$(1+2i)z+(2+i)(i)=4i$$

Evaluate the known product before isolating $z$.

$$\begin{aligned}(2+i)(i) &= (i)(2)+(i)(i) \\ &= 2i+i^2 \\ &= 2i+1(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= -1+2i\end{aligned}$$

Subtract the known term.

$$\begin{aligned}(1+2i)z&=(4i)-(-1+2i) \\ (1+2i)z&=1+2i\end{aligned}$$

Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate $1-2i$.

$$\begin{aligned}z &= \frac{1+2i}{1+2i} \\ &= \frac{1+2i}{1+2i}\cdot\frac{1-2i}{1-2i} && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \frac{1-2i}{1-2i}=1} \\ &= \frac{(1+2i)(1-2i)}{(1+2i)(1-2i)}\end{aligned}$$

Expand the numerator first.

$$\begin{aligned}(1+2i)(1-2i) &= 1(1)+1(-2i)+(2i)(1)+(2i)(-2i) \\ &= 1-2i+2i-4i^2 \\ &= 1-2i+2i-4(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 1-2i+2i+4 \\ &= (1+4)+(-2+2)i && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{collect like terms}} \\ &= 5\end{aligned}$$

Multiply the conjugate pair using the difference of squares.

$$\begin{aligned}(1+2i)(1-2i) &= 1^2-(2i)^2 && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small (a+b)(a-b)=a^2-b^2} \\ &= 1-4i^2 \\ &= 1-4(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 1+4 \\ &= 5\end{aligned}$$

Substitute the numerator and denominator, then simplify to rectangular form.

$$\begin{aligned}z &= \frac{5}{5} \\ &= 1\end{aligned}$$

Check the first original equation.

$$\begin{aligned}(1+2i)(1)+(2+i)(i) &= (1+2i)+(-1+2i) \\ &= 4i\end{aligned}$$

Check the second original equation with the same values.

$$\begin{aligned}(3-i)(1)+(1+i)(i) &= (3-i)+(-1+i) \\ &= 2\end{aligned}$$

Both equations are satisfied.

$$\begin{gathered}z=1 \\ w=i\end{gathered}$$
$z=1$ and $w=i$

1.q: Explain why $0$ is complex but is not purely imaginary under this unit’s nonzero convention.
1.solution:
Both coefficients in a complex number may be $0$.

$$0=0+0i$$

For a purely imaginary number, this unit requires $x=0$ and $y\neq0$. Here $y=0$, so $0$ is complex and real, but not purely imaginary.

$0=0+0i$ is complex. It fails the condition $y\ne0$ for purely imaginary numbers.

1.q: A student says that $z$ and $\bar z$ must be equal because $|z|=|\bar z|$. Give a counterexample.
1.solution:
Choose $z=1+2i$. Its conjugate is $1-2i$, so the two numbers are different. The real and imaginary coefficients are $1$ and $2$. Use the nonnegative square root.

$$\begin{aligned}|z| &= \sqrt{1^2+2^2} && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small |x+iy|=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}} \\ &= \sqrt{1+4} \\ &= \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}$$

The real and imaginary coefficients are $1$ and $-2$. Use the nonnegative square root.

$$\begin{aligned}|\bar z| &= \sqrt{1^2+(-2)^2} && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small |x+iy|=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}} \\ &= \sqrt{1+4} \\ &= \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}$$

The moduli agree, but the imaginary coefficients differ. This is a counterexample.

$$\begin{gathered}|z|=|\bar z|=\sqrt5 \\ z\neq\bar z\end{gathered}$$
$z=1+2i$, $\bar z=1-2i$; both moduli are $\sqrt{5}$, but the numbers differ.
1.answer_text: $z=1+2i$, $\bar z=1-2i$; both moduli are $\sqrt{5}$, but the numbers differ.

1.q: For real $x$, $\dfrac{x+2i}{1+i}$ is purely imaginary under the nonzero convention. Find $x$ and check that the resulting number is nonzero.
1.solution:
Use the conjugate $1-i$ to make the denominator real.

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{x+2i}{1+i} &= \frac{x+2i}{1+i}\cdot\frac{1-i}{1-i} \\ &= \frac{(x+2i)(1-i)}{(1+i)(1-i)}\end{aligned}$$

Multiply the conjugate pair using the difference of squares.

$$\begin{aligned}(1+i)(1-i) &= 1^2-i^2 && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small (a+b)(a-b)=a^2-b^2} \\ &= 1-i^2 \\ &= 1-1(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 1+1 \\ &= 2\end{aligned}$$

Expand the numerator, then collect its real and imaginary terms.

$$\begin{aligned}(x+2i)(1-i) &= x-xi+2i-2i^2 \\ &= x-xi+2i+2 && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= (x+2)+(2-x)i && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{collect like terms}}\end{aligned}$$

Put the numerator over the computed denominator.

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{x+2i}{1+i} &= \frac{(x+2)+(2-x)i}{2} \\ &= \frac{x+2}{2}+\frac{2-x}{2}i\end{aligned}$$

The denominator is nonzero. For a purely imaginary result, set the real coefficient equal to $0$.

$$\begin{aligned}x+2&=0 \\ x+2-2&=0-2 \\ x&=-2\end{aligned}$$

Check that the remaining imaginary coefficient is nonzero.

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{2-1(-2)}{2} &= \frac{4}{2} \\ &= 2\end{aligned}$$

This coefficient is nonzero, so the quotient is purely imaginary.

$x=-2$; the number is $2i$.

1.q: For real $x$, $\dfrac{x+3i}{2-i}$ is purely imaginary under the nonzero convention. Find $x$ and check that the resulting number is nonzero.
1.solution:
Use the conjugate $2+i$ to make the denominator real.

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{x+3i}{2-i} &= \frac{x+3i}{2-i}\cdot\frac{2+i}{2+i} \\ &= \frac{(x+3i)(2+i)}{(2-i)(2+i)}\end{aligned}$$

Multiply the conjugate pair using the difference of squares.

$$\begin{aligned}(2-i)(2+i) &= 2^2-i^2 && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small (a+b)(a-b)=a^2-b^2} \\ &= 4-i^2 \\ &= 4-1(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 4+1 \\ &= 5\end{aligned}$$

Expand the numerator, then collect its real and imaginary terms.

$$\begin{aligned}(x+3i)(2+i) &= 2x+xi+6i+3i^2 \\ &= 2x+xi+6i-3 && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= (2x-3)+(6+x)i && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{collect like terms}}\end{aligned}$$

Put the numerator over the computed denominator.

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{x+3i}{2-i} &= \frac{(2x-3)+(6+x)i}{5} \\ &= \frac{2x-3}{5}+\frac{6+x}{5}i\end{aligned}$$

The denominator is nonzero. For a purely imaginary result, set the real coefficient equal to $0$.

$$\begin{aligned}2x-3&=0 \\ 2x&=3 \\ x&=\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}$$

Check that the remaining imaginary coefficient is nonzero.

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{6-(-1)(\dfrac{3}{2})}{5} &= \frac{\dfrac{15}{2}}{5} \\ &= \dfrac{3}{2}\end{aligned}$$

This coefficient is nonzero, so the quotient is purely imaginary.

$x=\dfrac{3}{2}$; the number is $\dfrac{3}{2}i$.

1.q: For real $x$, $\dfrac{x+4i}{-1+2i}$ is purely imaginary under the nonzero convention. Find $x$ and check that the resulting number is nonzero.
1.solution:
Use the conjugate $-1-2i$ to make the denominator real.

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{x+4i}{-1+2i} &= \frac{x+4i}{-1+2i}\cdot\frac{-1-2i}{-1-2i} \\ &= \frac{(x+4i)(-1-2i)}{(-1+2i)(-1-2i)}\end{aligned}$$

Multiply the conjugate pair using the difference of squares.

$$\begin{aligned}(-1+2i)(-1-2i) &= (-1)^2-(2i)^2 && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small (a+b)(a-b)=a^2-b^2} \\ &= 1-4i^2 \\ &= 1-4(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 1+4 \\ &= 5\end{aligned}$$

Expand the numerator, then collect its real and imaginary terms.

$$\begin{aligned}(x+4i)(-1-2i) &= -x-2xi-4i-8i^2 \\ &= -x-2xi-4i+8 && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= (-x+8)+(-4-2x)i && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \text{collect like terms}}\end{aligned}$$

Put the numerator over the computed denominator.

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{x+4i}{-1+2i} &= \frac{(-x+8)+(-4-2x)i}{5} \\ &= \frac{-x+8}{5}+\frac{-4-2x}{5}i\end{aligned}$$

The denominator is nonzero. For a purely imaginary result, set the real coefficient equal to $0$.

$$\begin{aligned}-x+8&=0 \\ -x&=-8 \\ x&=8\end{aligned}$$

Check that the remaining imaginary coefficient is nonzero.

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{-4-2(8)}{5} &= \frac{-20}{5} \\ &= -4\end{aligned}$$

This coefficient is nonzero, so the quotient is purely imaginary.

$x=8$; the number is $-4i$.

1.q: For a nonzero complex number $z$, find the condition under which $z^{-1}=\bar z$. Justify it using $z\bar z=|z|^2$.
1.solution:
First suppose $z^{-1}=\bar z$. Since $z\neq0$, multiply by $z$.

$$\begin{gathered}zz^{-1}=z\bar z \\ 1=|z|^2\end{gathered}$$

A modulus is nonnegative, so taking its nonnegative square root gives

$$|z|=1$$

Conversely, suppose $|z|=1$. Then

$$z\bar z=|z|^2=1$$

Dividing by the nonzero number $z$ gives $\bar z=1/z=z^{-1}$. Thus the necessary and sufficient condition is

$$|z|=1$$
$|z|=1$.

1.q: A student claims $\mathrm{Re}(z^{-1})=1/\mathrm{Re}(z)$ whenever $\mathrm{Re}(z)\ne0$. Disprove this with one example.
1.solution:
Choose $z=1+i$, whose real part is $1\neq0$. Write the reciprocal and use the conjugate $1-i$.

$$\begin{aligned}z^{-1} &= \frac{1}{1+i} \\ &= \frac{1}{1+i}\cdot\frac{1-i}{1-i} && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small \frac{1-i}{1-i}=1} \\ &= \frac{1-i}{(1+i)(1-i)}\end{aligned}$$

Multiply the conjugate pair using the difference of squares.

$$\begin{aligned}(1+i)(1-i) &= 1^2-i^2 && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small (a+b)(a-b)=a^2-b^2} \\ &= 1-i^2 \\ &= 1-1(-1) && \textcolor{#40516D}{\small i^2=-1} \\ &= 1+1 \\ &= 2\end{aligned}$$

Substitute the numerator and denominator, then simplify to rectangular form.

$$\begin{aligned}z^{-1} &= \frac{1-i}{2} \\ &= \frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}i\end{aligned}$$

Compare the two quantities in the claim.

$$\begin{gathered}\operatorname{Re}(z^{-1})=\frac12 \\ \frac1{\operatorname{Re}(z)}=\frac11=1\end{gathered}$$

They differ, so this example disproves the claim.

For $z=1+i$, $\mathrm{Re}(z^{-1})=\dfrac{1}{2}$ but $1/\mathrm{Re}(z)=1$.
1.difficulty_reason: Choose and check a counterexample; the real-part operation does not commute with taking reciprocals.
